title: The Impact of ChatGPT as a Brainstorming Tool on Gifted Students’ Persuasive Writing
extended_summary:
This study examined whether using ChatGPT 3.5 as a prewriting brainstorming tool could improve the persuasive writing of gifted university students. The authors were motivated by concerns that gifted students, despite strong writing ability, may struggle with idea generation because of perfectionism and pressure to meet high expectations. They also sought to understand whether any writing gains would persist over time and how students perceived ChatGPT as a brainstorming support.

The intervention involved explicit instruction in using ChatGPT 3.5 for brainstorming only, not for drafting, editing, or translation. Students practiced asking ChatGPT questions to generate arguments, supporting evidence, counterarguments, and ways to present ideas. During intervention sessions, students read a prompt, brainstormed with ChatGPT for 20 minutes, then the internet was turned off and notes were collected before they independently wrote persuasive essays. The study used an integrated single-subject design with multiple probes across multiple baselines, and also included a focus group on social validity.

Participants were five gifted senior students majoring in Arabic at Kuwait University, all female and native Arabic speakers; four were typically developing and one was twice exceptional (gifted with high-functioning autism and depression). The study took place in a quiet, unoccupied classroom at Kuwait University during the 2023–2024 academic year. Group A completed three baseline probes, four intervention points, and one maintenance session; Group B completed five baseline probes, four intervention points, and one maintenance session. Maintenance occurred 3 weeks after intervention.

Results showed clear improvements in persuasive essay quality for all five participants from baseline to intervention, with mean score increases ranging from 30.7% to 68.1%. Gains were especially strong in persuasive-writing components such as argument quality, supporting evidence, opposing viewpoints, and voice/tone, while more general writing mechanics changed little. Four participants improved slightly further at maintenance, and one maintained intervention-level performance. Focus group responses suggested students viewed ChatGPT as efficient, idea-rich, and useful for discussing sensitive topics, while also recognizing limits such as outdated information, repetition, and possible cultural bias. Overall, the study concludes that ChatGPT 3.5 can function as a useful complementary brainstorming tool for gifted students’ persuasive writing, but should be used alongside other sources rather than relied on exclusively.

finding.finding_summary: Across all five participants, mean persuasive essay quality scores increased from baseline to intervention after ChatGPT was introduced as a brainstorming tool. Reported mean score changes were Hajar 29 to 40 (+37.9%), Maryam 26 to 34 (+30.7%), Tahany 24 to 38 (+58.3%), Asma' 23 to 36 (+56.5%), and Retaj 22 to 37 (+68.1%); the percentage of non-overlapping data (PND) was 100% for all five participants, which the authors interpret as documenting effectiveness.
finding.measure: Overall quality score on persuasive essays using an adapted Persuasive Essay Rubric (0-48 scale)

finding.finding_summary: Maintenance data collected 3 weeks after intervention showed continued improvement for four participants and stable maintenance for one participant. Mean maintenance scores were Hajar 41 (+2.5% from intervention), Maryam 35 (+2.9%), Tahany 39 (+2.6%), Asma' 36 (0%; unchanged from intervention), and Retaj 39 (+5.4%).
finding.measure: Maintenance-phase overall quality score on persuasive essays using an adapted Persuasive Essay Rubric (0-48 scale)
